prompt_text: Who is the best roofer in Denver for hail damage repair?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: There’s no single universally “best” roofer — the right one depends on your neighborhood, the size of the job, whether you want help with the insurance claim, and whether you prioritize warranty or price. I can help you pick the best contractor for your situation. To get you started, here’s a practical checklist and next steps so you can find a trustworthy Denver roofer for hail damage repair.

What to prioritize
- Hail/ storm experience: Look for contractors experienced with hail repairs and insurance claims.
- Insurance claim support: If you want help with your claim, choose a roofer who documents damage thoroughly and will coordinate with your adjuster.
- Manufacturer certifications: GAF, CertainTeed, Owens Corning, etc., indicate the roofer is trained and can offer extended warranties.
- Local reputation: High ratings and recent local references (Google, BBB, Yelp) matter more than national ads.
- Written warranty: Get both labor and material warranty details in writing.
- Proper insurance & licensing: Confirm the company carries liability insurance and workers’ comp; check local registration if required.
- Clear contract and scope: Price, materials, start/end dates, clean-up and how they handle unseen damage should be spelled out.

How to find good candidates
- Search Google Maps and filter by rating + recent reviews.
- Check the BBB profile and complaints history.
- Read recent Yelp/Google reviews, focusing on stories about hail repairs and claims support.
- Ask neighbors or HOA if others had hail repairs — local referrals are valuable.
- Avoid unexplained “storm chasers” who door-knock right after a storm and pressure you to sign immediately.

Questions to ask every roofer
1. How many hail-damage repairs have you completed in Denver in the last 12 months?
2. Are you manufacturer-certified (which brands)?
3. Will you meet with my insurance adjuster and provide a damage report/photos?
4. Do you provide a written warranty for labor and materials? How long?
5. Are you insured (liability and workers’ comp)? Can you provide certificates?
6. Do you use subcontractors and how are they vetted?
7. Can you provide local references with recent hail jobs?
8. What is your cleanup policy for nails/debris and do you use magnetic sweepers?

Red flags
- Unwillingness to provide proof of insurance or references.
- Asking for a very large up-front payment (standard is a small deposit).
- Only accepting cash or insisting you sign right away.
- Vague or no written contract.

If you want, I can:
- Draft a phone script or email you can use when contacting contractors.
- Help you compare 2–3 written estimates (if you share them).
- Recommend a short list of well-reviewed roofers in Denver if you give your ZIP code and whether you want contractors who handle insurance claims.

Which would you like next?
